sections.heading: 1. The dowel drill
lines: ① Stick on your back: head, upper back, tailbone.
② Soften the knees, push the hips back.
③ Feel the hamstrings stretch, stop, squeeze up.
④ 10 reps × 2 sets, all three points touching.

slides.heading: Worth an assessment if

caption:
Lulu lifts dozens of boxes on site every day, and her back feels heavy by knock-off.

The hip hinge means bending mainly from the hips, pushing them back while your chest tips forward. Try the broomstick drill: stick along your spine touching head, upper back and tailbone, soften the knees, push the hips back. When you feel the hamstrings stretch, squeeze your glutes and stand tall. Your back is allowed to round a little; the hinge just shares the load with your hips and legs.

If bending brings leg pain, numbness or weakness, get assessed first. Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physio can look at how you lift. Book online via the link in bio.
